title: NL Home Heating Supplement 2026: $200 to $500 for Oil Heat
desc: Newfoundland and Labrador pays a $200 to $500 supplement for furnace or stove oil. Apply by January 15, 2027 with your invoices. Income limit and how to apply.
h1: Newfoundland and Labrador Home Heating Supplement 2026-27
lead: If you heat your home with furnace or stove oil in Newfoundland and Labrador, the province pays a one-time supplement of $200 to $500. Applications close on January 15, 2027. Here is who can apply, what to bring and how it fits with the bigger Oil to Electric program.
cards_heading: What we found for Newfoundland and Labrador heating help
cards_intro: Each card names the official page we read on October 21, 2026. Dollar amounts are the government's own; anything it does not publish, we do not show.

cards.title: Home Heating Supplement
cards.note: For residents who directly pay for furnace or stove oil to heat their main home. Open for applications until January 15, 2027.

sections: Who can apply

You must directly pay for furnace or stove oil to heat your principal residence. The province sets a 2025 adjusted family income cap of $150,000 or less. You need invoices that show your delivery address and at least 250 litres of furnace or stove oil, and a signed application with a correct Social Insurance Number.
The deadline
Applications are open until January 15, 2027. Do not wait for the last week. Gather your invoices now, since they are the part that takes time.
How to get help
Email OilSupplement@gov.nl.ca, or call 709-729-4645 or toll-free 1-844-729-4645. The program page is on the Government of Newfoundland and Labrador site under Finance.
What we cannot confirm
A search summary said the $500 level applies at $100,000 of income or less and slides toward $200 above that. We did not read that, so we do not state how the amount slides. Ask the program.
Think about the bigger fix

Oil heat costs a lot to run. The Oil to Electric program from takeCHARGE pays up to $22,000 for lower-income households switching to a central heat pump, with $9,000 for the general program. See the Newfoundland pages below for who qualifies.
Keep your invoices
Save every oil invoice with your address on it. Photocopies are fine. If a delivery is missing an address, ask your supplier to reissue it before you apply.
Who counts as an oil heater

The supplement is for people who directly pay for furnace or stove oil. If your landlord pays for the oil and you do not, ask the program whether you can apply. We did not read a rule on this, so we do not say.
Plan your litres

You need at least 250 litres on your invoices. Many households buy in smaller loads during the winter. Add up your invoices to check before you send them in, and ask your supplier for a summary if you made many small buys.
Do it now, not in January

The deadline is January 15, 2027, but oil use is highest in the coldest months, and invoices from those months are the easiest to collect. Applying earlier gives you time to fix a mistake, such as a missing address on an invoice or an incorrect SIN.
Heat pump upgrades

If your oil furnace is old, the Oil to Electric program can pay up to $22,000 for lower-income households. A heat pump can also cool the home in summer. Read the program page and the St. John's page for the rules and the open status.
Keep a copy

Make a copy of your signed form and your invoices before you send them in. If the program asks a question months later, you will have the same papers in front of you. Write down the date you applied and keep any confirmation you receive. It also helps to note the name of anyone you spoke with at the program.

faq: How much is the Home Heating Supplement?
$200 to $500, for people who directly pay for furnace or stove oil.
A 2025 adjusted family income of $150,000 or less.
Invoices with your delivery address for at least 250 litres of furnace or stove oil.
